Clouded Eye Clan (B24)

Scoring-table region: Escann.

In brief: A wise orc clan amid the Greentide builds its own cities, laws, and multi-ethnic home instead of continuing to fight wars of plunder for the Dookanson.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 72/100 | Authoritarianism 55/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 90/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 48/100) | Pluralism 82/100. Phase trajectory: Grama's Greentide clan (Authoritarianism 68, Pluralism 35) → Arosha's urban community (Authoritarianism 50, Pluralism 85). The v2.1 values score is Good (79/100), with an improving trajectory. Phase values: Grama's Greentide clan (Neutral, 54/100) → Arosha's urban community (Good, 79/100). Equality among half-orcs and humans, fewer pointless warrior deaths, and urban development provide strong positive evidence; revenge against the Bladebreakers and repression during reform reduce restraint. War and orcish identity themselves do not enter the good/evil score. Phase values: Grama's Greentide clan (Neutral, 54/100) → Arosha's urban community (Good, 79/100).

Narrative: high | Mission tree: medium-long (25 Clouded Eye-specific definitions, plus shared orc missions) | Mission-tree update: use the local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 as the reference | Distinctiveness: high | Tedium: medium (opening land grabs, reforms, and local backlash) | Early pressure: high | Expansion capacity: medium-high.

Identity and History

In 1444, the Clouded Eye is a Green Orc tribe in Escann, following Great Dookan and retaining the Greentide tribal reform. It is ruled by Grama Clouded Eye; a footnote in the local country history calls her Korgus's senior shaman and non-military adviser, who helped organize the Greentide. Her authority comes from foresight and strategy, not only physical strength. 【Local history script】

The English offline Wiki describes the Clouded Eye as a clan known for shamans, sages, and mystical relics. It recounts that after Grama, Arosha Oakbreaker took over the clan, abandoned the teachings of the Dookanson, and eventually established Unguldavor. But this Wiki account is written with hindsight: Grama's government in 1444 and the missions' future must not be collapsed into “Arosha has already founded a kingdom.” The Wiki's Greentide-history section itself says it remains unfinished, so a detailed chronology of the campaign should not be inferred from it. 【Wiki】

National Story and Campaign Arc

The Clouded Eye's distinctive premise lets you play a clan that believes orcs can think, negotiate, and build cities. Its missions first seek a foothold among the Bladebreakers, the Dog Clans, and human powers; they turn the Ardent Keep into a real city, then gradually build institutions for writing, administration, military affairs, and education. The mission text does not define orcish civilization as abandoning orcish identity; instead, it tries to combine clan traditions with the organizational capacity of settled society. 【Local narrative text】

The relationships among Arosha, Corin, and Lothane move the story from “Greentide remnants trying to survive” toward a different order in Escann. The clearest turning point is “A New People”: on a route where humans and orcs can live as equals, half-orcs cease to be merely scars left by war and become members of the country. Dagom urban politics then rises, but reform also angers those committed to the old clan ways. Revenge against the Bladebreakers is especially severe; this path should not be reduced to idealism without a violent cost. 【Local narrative text】

Core Mechanics and Gameplay

At the start, war and settlement are still necessary to secure space. “Our First City” makes control and development of the Ardent Keep a campaign hub. “A New People” links population, culture, and provincial development to a half-orc community; “Promote the Dagom” brings both development gains and local backlash into state governance. Shamanic tradition and the relic known as the Clouded Eye bring prophecy and mysticism, but the central loop is not unlimited spellcasting: it is the transition from nomadic warfare to an urban state. 【Local script】【Local narrative text】

Forming Unguldavor (Z52) is a possible later national transition. The current decision lets eligible Green or Grey Orc countries form it in Inner Cannor; it is not a button exclusive to the Clouded Eye. Formation changes the Tag and mission tree, while the formable's missions also check whether the country was formerly B24, preserving a special continuation for the Clouded Eye route. Do not count all Z52 missions as exclusive B24 content or treat the Wiki's kingdom account as an inevitable player ending. 【Local script】

Personality and Recommendation

The provisional v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansionism 72 | Authoritarianism 55 | Magic-oriented 90, theme intensity 48 | Pluralism 82. Its values tendency is Good (79, improving): missions explicitly support an equal community of humans, orcs, and half-orcs and seek to reduce pointless losses among its own warriors. Brutal revenge against an enemy and internal conflict during reform lower its restraint score. War, orcish identity, and tribal government are not themselves treated as evidence of good or evil.

Recommended for players who enjoy orcish reconstruction, inherited characters, half-orc society, urbanization, and a continuous campaign into a formable state. If you only want to roll across the map with Greentide cavalry and have little patience for city-building or reform backlash, the Clouded Eye demands more attention than its appearance suggests.

Community Experience and Evidence Boundaries

The official 2025 Dev Diary explicitly presents the Clouded Eye as a story of cooperation and reconstruction. Two 2026 player discussions say the mission tree feels complete, while warning that the Count's League may occupy the Ardent Keep first. These are version-dependent experiences and cannot replace the current mission conditions. 【Official Dev Diary】【Community opinion】

Local scripts determine identity, formation, and mechanics; the current Chinese localization determines the in-game display name; the offline Wiki adds context about Grama, Arosha, and clan traditions. Exact line references, Wiki revisions, and player posts are on the evidence page.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Clouded Eye (B24) — Clouded Eye Ideas

Set ID: B24_ideas_rc. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B24
        has_country_flag = ce_regent_court
    }

Clouded Eye Traditions

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1).

  • Fort defense: +20% (defensiveness; raw value 0.20).

1. Truesight of the Blind

For generations our sagely shamans have sacrificed their very vision in an ancient clan ritual known as "The Trial of Clouded", all in the pursuit of Dookan’s wisdom. The ritual is a dangerous one, but those who survive find themselves better attuned with shamanic magics. A worthy few may even wield "The Clouded Eye", a mystical object consisting of a rough uncut gem of pure glowing white crystal. A treasure our clan has long guarded, the Eye is believed to have been gifted directly from Dookan and may even be the eye of the chained god himself. With the power to bestow great visions of a possible future and detail insights on the lore of the past, what other origin could there be?

  • All power costs: -2.5% (all_power_cost; raw value -0.025).

2. Legacy of Grama

While other clans may sing of bold and mighty warchiefs, we instead honor the wise and clever; none other embodies this better than our legendary chieftain, Grama. It was her prophetic dream of the verdant lands outside that led us to rally behind Korgus as one of his first and most fervent followers. It was her clever tongue that settled disputes between the clans as the Greentide swept from Castellyr to Farranaen, carving apart the old kingdoms of Escann. It was her guile at Rottenstep that left the Aldresians decimated under the might of our shamans. And when The Dookanson fell, it was she who led us to the rich hills of Gulenhyl where our people may bring life to the vision she had so many years ago. Even after she draws her final breath, we know that it will be her teachings that will guide us toward our new future.

  • Improve relations: +10% (improve_relation_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Prestige: +0.5 (prestige; raw value 0.50).

3. Embracing a New Era

With the death of beloved Grama and the increasing pressure faced from the adventurer onslaught, our seers desperately scoured our clan for a leader, a new warchief who could lead us to glory and unite the clans torn asunder by Dookansfall. Yet as we divined the fates of our fiercest warriors and wisest shamans, despair began to set in. Every orc, from the descendants of Grama herself to the seasoned veterans of the Greentide, was doomed to meet their end by the adventurer's blade or by the slaver's chain.

Then she came.

Clad in the armor reminiscent of our adventurer foes and mighty axe in hand, Arosha of the disgraced Oakbreakers would arrive in Clouded Eye to much commotion. After leaving any warrior who challenged her sprawled on the ground, Arosha called out to the shamans of our clan. With a bellow, the warrior gave voice to the lessons learned in her exile. Lessons from her once companion, Corin Korguskiller. That strength and honor were made whole by duty and compassion.

When Arosha had finished, the gathered shamans did not respond at first. Nor did they attempt to divine with magic or invoke the Clouded Eye. Instead, they kneeled. For the first time since Grama’s death, the future was clear. Ushering in the era of Arosha Oakbreaker, Chieftain of Clouded Eye.

  • Stability cost modifier: -20% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.2).

4. Tuladosh

The decades after the Greentide’s ultimate defeat and Korgus Dookanson’s death would be a chaotic one for the Escanni orcs. For two decades, ultimate authority had been centralised around Korgus and his divine connection to Dookan. His downfall did not simply shatter orcish unity, it left a power vacuum within the clans themselves as many chieftains had tied their own legitimacy to Korgus’ (and by extension Dookan’s) will.

Roughly equivalent to the idiom of "ruling with an iron fist", Tuladosh, or steel hand, represented the various Escanni orcish chieftains bids to assert firmer control over their clans. Some would attempt to take up Korgus’ fallen mantle in a bid for legitimacy. Others would focus their efforts on rebuilding the ruined land to build trust. More still would settle for trying to dominate the local surroundings to show their strength. All would find their efforts a struggle.

  • global_autonomy：-0.05% (global_autonomy; raw value -0.05).

5. The Dargom and Ozdan

As the Green Orcs transitioned from conquerors to inhabitants, two classes would come to form within the various nascent kingdoms - the Dargom and Ozdan. Residing within the rebuilt hamlets and refounded towns, the Dargom represented the evolution of orcish society.

Dominated by craftspeople, merchants and other urban roles, the Dargom stemmed from those who already held great wealth and power or recognized the power that could come from craftsmanship and commerce. Through these means, the Dargom would form the basis of the nascent bureaucracy and come to control much of the state’s wealth.

The Ozdan, on the other hand, represented unchanging orcish tradition. Dominated by travelling warriors and migratory herders who were either too poor (or too stubborn) to settle, the Ozdan’s hearty lifestyle meant they were a natural pool to draw on for the kingdom’s defence. While capable, their adherence to the old ways would lead constant headaches to the central government

  • Production efficiency: +5% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

  • global_manpower_modifier：+7.5% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.075).

6. Beyond the Ebbing Tide

While the animosity between the orcs of Escann and the other races would last generations as the struggle for land continued into the 16th century, old hatred would eventually give way to cold utilitarianism.

Heralding this evolution would be the Crimson Deluge, a seemingly divine cataclysm that showered Escann with blood and gore. With these unnatural events came disruptions to commerce as tumultuous weather began to claim Escanni caravans. As an economic crisis began to brew, it would be the orcish kingdoms who would step in. Orcs, stronger than the average human and born wayfinders, were more capable of withstanding the treacherous rains and the violence it wrought. While initially rejected, the merchants of Cannor found themselves more willing to look the other way and allow orcs to trek these treacherous routes as long as the coin flowed.

  • Global institution spread: +10% (global_institution_spread; raw value 0.1).

  • Ruler culture advisor cost: -7.5% (same_culture_advisor_cost; raw value -0.075).

7. Sagah'dams

Whatever equilibrium that arose between the adventurer kingdoms and orcish kingdoms would come to a violent end when the first witch kings arose. Armies onto themselves, the orcish kingdoms buckled under the likes of mages like Laurens síl Place and the Regent of Wyvernheart. When even the most powerful shamans were reduced to dust in the face of such foes, it was clear new tactics had to be adopted.

What came about was the sagah’dams, or shadowshots. Taking advantage of their skin’s natural camouflage in the greenery of Escann, these warriors would rely on ambush tactics to inhibit and blunt ever more brazen advances into orcish land. As these brave orcs fought to preserve their home, some could not help but find it ironic it was they who were now being swept away by some unstoppable tide…

  • Hostile Attrition: +100% (hostile_attrition; raw value 1).

Clouded Eye Ambitions

  • Army tradition: +1 (army_tradition; raw value 1).
